name: Orbit AI - Phase 0 - Automation failure watchdog (new, not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Every hour
nodes.notes: 05 Section 11: '...automation/workflow failure monitoring (meta watchdog on n8n execution failures).' Deliberately DIFFERENT from every workflow's own `settings.errorWorkflow` field - that per-workflow setting is defense LAYER ONE (a failure alerts, assuming errorWorkflow is actually configured correctly on that specific workflow after import). This is layer two: an outside check against n8n's own Executions API that catches a failure even if a workflow's errorWorkflow was never set, was misconfigured, or the alert-dispatcher chain itself broke - the exact 'meta' framing the brief uses, watching n8n's execution history rather than depending on each workflow to self-report.

nodes.name: Fetch failed executions
nodes.notes: n8n's own public REST API (api/v1, X-N8N-API-KEY header), NOT Twenty CRM's - this is the one workflow in this library that queries the automation platform itself rather than the CRM. N8N_API_KEY is already a named credential in this library's own 'Credential naming' section (workflows/README.md) and the Command Center vendor checklist - reused here, not invented. UNVERIFIED: the exact endpoint path/query params against a real n8n instance's public API version - built from n8n's documented API shape, not exercised live.

nodes.name: Any failures in the last hour?
Alert: automation failures detected

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'critical', source: 'automation-failure-watchdog', message: $json.failureCount + ' workflow execution(s) failed in the last hour: ' + $json.summary + '.' }) }}

nodes.notes: Critical, not warning - this fires only after already confirming a real failure happened (not a prediction or a threshold guess), and a silently-broken automation is exactly the kind of thing that erodes trust in 'the system just handles it' if it goes unnoticed. Routes to #system-alerts (alertRouting.ts's fallback channel, which this source doesn't match any more specific rule for - correctly so, since this genuinely IS an infra/ops concern per 05 Section 14's own description of that channel).
